teacher_explanatory_note_or_risk: Fluid identification is Knowledge-level prerequisite; source not automatically certifiable as B33 Application.
Pressure rise with depth for static constant-density fluid; can be framed as model prerequisite.
Bottom deeper than top in ordinary static water; a horizontal top/bottom face geometry is assumed.
Naming upthrust tests recall rather than application of Archimedes principle.
Direction of net hydrostatic buoyancy is vertical; recall demand is below B33 Application.
Formula FB=rho_fluid*g*V_displaced is correct; select-expression item does not independently demonstrate Application.
Equals volume for rigid impenetrable block that is completely submerged; pores/cavities require care.
Newton is force SI unit; low cognitive demand relative to B33 official Application.
P=rho*g*h is hydrostatic pressure increase relative to the free surface for constant density; absolute P also includes surface pressure.
F=PA on a planar face with approximately uniform pressure. Static liquid pressure force on horizontal top acts downward.
F2=P2*A; educational V93 Figure6.2 was independently matched; do not copy the original textbook figure or claim full printed-source fidelity.
h=h2-h1 for h2>h1, common vertical depth datum.
F_B=F2-F1 in symmetric equal-face-area static cylinder model; lateral vertical components cancel. Does not describe every arbitrary shape with only two faces.
V=A*h for a uniform-area cylinder (or prism) with its full body volume represented; displaced volume equals this only if fully immersed.
Displaced-fluid weight, not body weight, equals buoyancy in Archimedes principle; recall-level selection.
FB=W gives zero vertical resultant only when no other vertical forces and no vertical acceleration; an initially moving object need not be instantly stationary.
Admitting sea water changes total carried mass/weight and mean density, assuming water replaces tank air and hull geometry approximately fixed.
Ballast seawater is expelled, typically with compressed air; air supply depends on equipment rather than atmospheric air at depth.
Water displaced provides ship buoyancy matching total loaded ship weight at floating equilibrium, not stability or seaworthiness alone.
Low centre of gravity/ballast assist stability but righting stability also depends on hull geometry and loading. No real seaworthiness certification.
